newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close firmer, helped by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close firmer, helped by bonds.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Tuesday, buoyed by a firm lira and a steady bonds market, as San Paolo, Pirelli and Telecom Italia Mobile led the upward trend.
* The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.66 percent higher at 12,238 with the blue-chip Mib30 index finishing the day 0.75 percent higher at 18,212.

* Brokers said that despite market uncertainty over EMU developments, the French socialists' election victory and the German gold row were seen probably increasing Italy's chances of taking part in a broad-based currency union.

* San Paolo outperformed the banks, finishing three percent higher at 10,953 lire, rebounding after the completion of the public share offer. The share price had drifted down ahead of the fixing of the offer price last month.

* TIM closed 2.06 percent higher at 5,101 lire on a technical recovery. The stock has been hit recently by fears that its margins will come under pressure with the entry of a third operator in the mobile phones market.
* The government has said that it will invite bids for a third licence later this month.
* Fiat closed 1.01 percent higher at 5,709 lire and Pirelli advanced 1.92 percent to 3,830 lire. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
